section_summary: This section begins with 1945 correspondence locating Japanese textile mills and assessing wartime damage to textile machinery. Most subsequent documents concern plans for an Allied survey of Japan’s textile industry, requests from American manufacturers and traders, and invitations to British, Chinese and Indian observers. Pages 62–80 begin a longer Foreign Economic Administration report on Japan’s textile production, controls and raw material needs.

subfiles.title: Suggested reply to Edward E. I. Martin
subfiles.about: Locates Japanese spinning mills and assesses textile machinery losses.
subfiles.summary: Gives regional mill concentrations and town locations, discusses machinery scrapping and factory conversion, and doubts Japan will soon recover its prewar cotton export position.

subfiles.title: Letter on Japanese textile plants
subfiles.about: Answers an inquiry about mill locations and wartime damage.
subfiles.summary: Provides a regional inventory of spinning mills and estimates that late 1944 operating cotton spindles were at most one quarter of the 1939 number.

subfiles.title: British proposal for a textile commission
subfiles.about: Forwards Sansom’s proposal for a combined textile investigation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks Clayton’s office to formulate the Department’s view.

subfiles.title: Proposed combined investigation of Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Requests State Department support for a combined technical commission.
subfiles.summary: Seeks prompt information on stocks, production capacity, reparations and future exports.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Sir George Sansom
subfiles.about: Refers the commission proposal to Clayton’s office.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Sansom’s letter and offers informal assistance.

subfiles.title: Reply on proposed technical mission
subfiles.about: Describes arrangements to obtain information on Japan’s textile industry.
subfiles.summary: Says the inquiry will consider world shortages and the interests of major textile producers and consumers.

subfiles.title: Recommended response to William Batt
subfiles.about: Recommends delaying a combined mission until occupation conditions permit a useful survey.
subfiles.summary: Proposes an eventual international technical mission and interim economic reporting from Japan.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Sir George Sansom
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the British proposal for a textile investigation.
subfiles.summary: States that Clayton’s office will formulate the Department’s opinion.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Japanese textile policy
subfiles.about: Forwards a manufacturer’s inquiry about Japanese textile plants and U.S. policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests information and return of the enclosure.

subfiles.title: Manufacturer’s concerns about Japanese cotton textiles
subfiles.about: Asks about bomb damage and future Japanese cotton textile competition.
subfiles.summary: Urges limits on Japanese production and questions subsidized exports.

subfiles.title: Reply to Stephen Pace
subfiles.about: Responds to Pace’s request for information on Japan’s textile industry.
subfiles.summary: Says no official inventory is complete and returns the enclosure.

subfiles.title: Interim acknowledgment to Stephen Pace
subfiles.about: Promises to seek information requested by E. W. Swift.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Swift’s letter and promises a later reply.

subfiles.title: Raw Silk Control Association to continue
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese plans to retain raw silk controls and reserve stocks for export.
subfiles.summary: Quotes Yamazoe on control, 60,000 bales of stocks and uncertain production.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese textile industry information
subfiles.about: Seeks reliable spindle figures and U.S. plans for Japanese textile production.
subfiles.summary: Challenges conflicting reports, asks for a plant survey and policy disclosure, and offers industry experts.

subfiles.title: Clayton’s note on proposed reply
subfiles.about: Requests review of a response before signature.
subfiles.summary: Asks to see the response before signing it.

subfiles.title: Routing to Martin
subfiles.about: Routes the textile inquiry for action.
subfiles.summary: Marks the matter for appropriate action.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to William C. Planz
subfiles.about: Promises to seek information and consider the offer of survey personnel.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Planz’s inquiry and assistance offer.

subfiles.title: Substantive reply to William C. Planz
subfiles.about: Explains occupation control and the proposed expert mission.
subfiles.summary: Says MacArthur controls Japanese trade, a mission may establish reliable industry facts, and personnel nominations can go to the War Department.

subfiles.title: Offer to purchase Japanese textile waste
subfiles.about: Inquires about Japanese cotton, rayon and staple fiber waste stocks.
subfiles.summary: Offers to buy available waste and send an employee to grade it.

subfiles.title: Reply on textile waste exports
subfiles.about: Responds to an inquiry about Japanese textile waste.
subfiles.summary: Says stock figures are unavailable, occupation authorities will be notified, and business travel remains restricted.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation file note
subfiles.about: Refers a matter to Martin following a telephone conversation.
subfiles.summary: A brief, partly illegible routing note.

subfiles.title: Referral of wool trade inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards Ilfeld’s wool import inquiry and the bank’s reply.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies after a telephone discussion.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about wool imports for Japan
subfiles.about: Asks how his firm could participate in supplying Australian wool to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Seeks a responsible agency and concrete guidance on future purchases.

subfiles.title: Export-Import Bank reply to Ilfeld
subfiles.about: Refers the wool import inquiry to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Says the bank lacks information on the subject.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Japanese wool imports
subfiles.about: Explains restrictions on Japanese imports during occupation.
subfiles.summary: No raw wool imports have been approved or are expected soon; future arrangements will be announced publicly.

subfiles.title: Survey of the North China cotton textile industry
subfiles.about: Summarizes mill capacity, cotton stocks, production and controls in North China.
subfiles.summary: Reports severe raw cotton shortages, largely idle Japanese mills, limited Chinese mill operation and wartime Japanese controls over cotton collection and textile distribution.

subfiles.title: Chinese inquiry about textile mission participation
subfiles.about: Reports China’s proposed representative for a Japan weaving survey.
subfiles.summary: Names Yang Hoi Jen and requests instructions before arranging transport or contacting occupation headquarters.

subfiles.title: Invitation to India to observe the textile mission
subfiles.about: Invites an Indian observer to the proposed Japanese textile survey.
subfiles.summary: Explains the mission’s purpose, composition, expected duration and tentative departure.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Embassy Chongqing on textile mission
subfiles.about: Confirms the mission plan while warning that departure will be delayed.
subfiles.summary: Reproduces the invitation to China and promises a confirmed departure date after occupation clearance.

subfiles.title: Travel instructions to Maxwell W. Becker
subfiles.about: Gives tentative departure and passport instructions.
subfiles.summary: Sets a tentative 15 December departure and directs an official passport application.

subfiles.title: Invitation to Britain to observe the textile mission
subfiles.about: Invites a British observer to the proposed Japanese textile survey.
subfiles.summary: Explains the mission’s purpose, composition, expected duration and tentative departure.

subfiles.title: Invitation to China to observe the textile mission
subfiles.about: Invites a Chinese observer to the proposed Japanese textile survey.
subfiles.summary: Explains the mission’s purpose, composition, expected duration and tentative departure.

subfiles.title: Rose on mission departure timing
subfiles.about: Proposes a 27 December departure for the textile mission.
subfiles.summary: Says Rose, Comer and Rowe are ready and plan a Washington meeting.

subfiles.title: Correction to Rose’s departure letter
subfiles.about: Corrects the proposed date in Rose’s earlier letter.
subfiles.summary: Changes “the 22nd” to “the 27th.”

subfiles.title: India accepts observer invitation
subfiles.about: Names India’s representative and requests transport for him and his secretary.
subfiles.summary: Accepts the invitation, nominates Bharat Ram and asks that M. D. Parekh accompany him.

subfiles.title: Britain accepts observer invitation
subfiles.about: Names Britain’s observer on the Japanese textile mission.
subfiles.summary: Accepts the invitation and nominates F. S. Winterbottom.

subfiles.title: Information on Shunosuke Yoshimoto
subfiles.about: Passes along an unverified suggestion for silk export supervision.
subfiles.summary: Describes Yoshimoto’s business background and family connection, without recommending his appointment.

subfiles.title: Invitation to Hugh Comer
subfiles.about: Invites Comer to serve on the U.S. textile mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Explains the survey’s policy purpose and says the War Department will arrange travel details.

subfiles.title: Invitation to Frank E. Rowe Jr.
subfiles.about: Invites Rowe to serve on the U.S. textile mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Explains the need to assess Japanese production and imports and promises travel arrangements.

subfiles.title: Invitation to H. Wickliffe Rose
subfiles.about: Invites Rose to serve on the U.S. textile mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sets out the survey’s purpose, reporting route and expected travel arrangements.

subfiles.title: Rowe accepts textile mission assignment
subfiles.about: Confirms preparations for the Japan textile mission.
subfiles.summary: Promises to gather facts and welcomes Fred Taylor’s participation.

subfiles.title: Travel instructions to Hugh Comer
subfiles.about: Provides San Francisco reporting and travel instructions.
subfiles.summary: Covers route, expenses, passport revision, possible China travel and mission address.

subfiles.title: Travel instructions to Frank E. Rowe Jr.
subfiles.about: Provides luggage and mail address instructions.
subfiles.summary: Directs Rowe to check luggage limits in his orders.

subfiles.title: Transmission of report EIS-93
subfiles.about: Transmits a report on the Japanese textile industry.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a copy of EIS-93.

subfiles.title: The Japanese Textile Industry
subfiles.about: Studies Japanese textile production, wartime controls, processing capacity and raw material supplies.
subfiles.summary: The report cautions that its recommendations were drafted before Japan’s surrender. Its opening sections describe the industry’s prewar export importance, wartime conversion of mills, reduced silk output, and dependence on imported cotton, wool, pulp and salt. It estimates potential postwar supplies of natural, industrial and synthetic fibers and discusses the machinery, chemical, coal and transport constraints facing occupation planners. The report continues beyond page 80.
